overview: White offers the c-pawn with 2.c4 against the Dutch-reversed set-up, hoping for fast development and f4/c4 play against Black's centre. After 2...dxc4 Black can keep the pawn but must be careful about the e-file and the exposed king. It is a rare gambit and not considered fully sound.

white_ideas.idea: Develop quickly with Nf3, e3 and Bxc4
Use the f-pawn and open d- and e-files against the king

black_ideas.idea: Keep the extra pawn and trade pieces
Return the pawn for solid development when needed

typical_structures.structure: Open or semi-open centre after cxd5 or ...dxc4 lines

character.notes: White sacrifices a pawn and the f4 move weakens the king, so both sides must calculate and a slip loses fast.

gambit.notes: White offers c4 and Black can keep it with ...dxc4.

soundness.notes: Strong players consider the compensation insufficient, but it is a mild one.

structure.notes: After ...dxc4 and e3 the centre is open with the d- and e-files and bishops in play.

approach.notes: Chosen mostly for surprise and rarely seen among strong players.

level.notes: A dubious gambit is not a first repertoire choice, so Intermediate.

sublines_that_differ.name: 2...e6
sublines_that_differ.how: Declining; the gambit is gone and play is normal.
